regional.syndrome: Sudden high fever with severe, often symmetrical polyarthralgia and rash; the name means 'that which bends up'. Arthritis persists for months to years in 30–40%. Neonatal infection from intrapartum transmission and neurological disease in older adults can be severe; deaths occur mainly via decompensation of comorbidity.
regional.headline: Alphavirus of the Semliki Forest complex causing explosive epidemics of febrile polyarthritis.
regional.prevention: Vector control; the virus-like particle vaccine Vimkunya is licensed from 12 years of age. The live-attenuated IXCHIQ was licensed first, but its US licence was suspended in August 2025 and the application withdrawn in January 2026 after vaccine-strain encephalitis and other serious adverse events.
regional.geography: Africa, Asia, Indian Ocean, Americas since 2013, with autochthonous outbreaks in southern Europe.
regional.evidence_note: Human infection has been confirmed in this country.

regional.syndrome: Dengue fever: high fever, severe headache, retro-orbital pain, myalgia/arthralgia ('breakbone fever'), rash. A minority progress at defervescence to dengue with warning signs or severe dengue — plasma leakage, shock, haemorrhage and organ impairment. Secondary infection with a different serotype raises severe-disease risk through antibody-dependent enhancement.
regional.headline: The most important arboviral infection of humans worldwide, with an estimated 100–400 million infections annually.
regional.prevention: Vector control, Wolbachia-based mosquito replacement, and the live-attenuated vaccines CYD-TDV (serostatus-restricted) and TAK-003.
regional.geography: Tropics and subtropics worldwide; expanding with vector range.
regional.evidence_note: Human infection has been confirmed in this country.

regional.syndrome: About 80% of infections are asymptomatic; 20% develop West Nile fever; <1% develop neuroinvasive disease — meningitis, encephalitis or a poliomyelitis-like acute flaccid paralysis, with substantial mortality and long-term sequelae in older adults.
regional.headline: Globally the most widespread encephalitic flavivirus, maintained in a bird–mosquito cycle.
regional.prevention: Mosquito control and personal protection; blood-supply nucleic-acid screening; equine vaccines exist but no human vaccine.
regional.geography: Africa, Europe, Middle East, Asia, Australia (Kunjin), and across the Americas since 1999.
regional.evidence_note: Human infection has been confirmed in this country.

regional.syndrome: Usually mild or asymptomatic: low-grade fever, maculopapular rash, conjunctivitis, arthralgia. Congenital Zika syndrome — microcephaly, cerebral calcification, ocular and joint anomalies — follows infection in pregnancy. Guillain–Barré syndrome is an established post-infectious complication.
regional.headline: Flavivirus whose 2015–2016 American epidemic established it as a human teratogen.
regional.prevention: Vector control, barrier contraception or abstinence after exposure, travel advice in pregnancy. No licensed vaccine.
regional.evidence_note: Human infection has been confirmed in this country.

regional.syndrome: A short prodrome of fever and myalgia, then abrupt non-cardiogenic pulmonary oedema and cardiogenic shock; case fatality ~35–40%. Renal involvement is minimal, in contrast to HFRS.
regional.headline: Cause of hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome in North America, identified during the 1993 Four Corners outbreak.
regional.prevention: Rodent-proofing and safe cleaning practice (wet methods, no sweeping). No vaccine.
regional.geography: Western and central United States, Canada, Mexico.
regional.evidence_note: Human infection has been confirmed in this country.

regional.headline: Vesicular stomatitis Indiana virus. Influenza-like illness in exposed livestock and laboratory workers.
regional.geography: Vesicular stomatitis Indiana virus. Influenza-like illness in exposed livestock and laboratory workers.
regional.evidence_note: Human infection has been confirmed in this country.

regional.headline: Vesicular stomatitis New Jersey virus. Influenza-like occupational illness.
regional.geography: Vesicular stomatitis New Jersey virus. Influenza-like occupational illness.
regional.evidence_note: Human infection has been confirmed in this country.

regional.syndrome: Rare but documented human meningoencephalitis and multi-organ disease, including fatal cases; mild febrile illness is likely far more common. In sheep, it causes abortion and congenital malformation.
regional.headline: North American Bunyamwera-serogroup virus; a teratogen in sheep and a rare cause of severe human neuroinvasive disease.
regional.evidence_note: Human infection has been confirmed in this country.

regional.syndrome: Abrupt febrile illness ('Oropouche fever') with severe headache, myalgia, arthralgia, chills, photophobia and nausea; frequently relapsing after a few days of apparent recovery. Aseptic meningitis and meningoencephalitis occur. Vertical transmission with fetal loss and congenital anomalies reported during the 2024 expansion, as well as rare fatalities.
regional.headline: The most important human pathogen of the Simbu serogroup and, after dengue, one of the most frequent arboviral febrile illnesses in the Amazon basin. Major expansion across the Americas from 2023–2024.
regional.prevention: Midge control is difficult (C. paraensis is tiny and bites outdoors by day); fine-mesh screening, repellents, reduction of peridomestic breeding (decaying banana/cacao debris).
regional.geography: Amazon basin — Brazil, Peru, Bolivia, Ecuador, Colombia, Panama, Trinidad; marked 2024 expansion including Cuba and travel-associated cases exported to Europe and North America.
regional.evidence_note: Human infection has been confirmed in this country.

regional.headline: Western equine encephalitis virus. Encephalitis in the Americas.
regional.geography: Western equine encephalitis virus. Encephalitis in the Americas.
regional.evidence_note: Human infection has been confirmed in this country.

regional.headline: St. Louis encephalitis virus. Encephalitis outbreaks in the Americas.

regional.evidence_note: Human infection has been confirmed in this country.
